every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Amitriptyline, a lipophilic tricyclic tertiary amine with a dimethylaminopropyl side chain, has human oral bioavailability values of 40-60% (C04), 46±48% (C07), 48±11% (C12), and 47.7±11.0% (C19), demonstrating that a similar lipophilic basic amine can exceed the 20% F threshold.

Alfentanil, a lipophilic anilino/piperidine opioid, has human oral F of 37% (C01), 0.45±0.09 (C11), and 0.42±0.15 (C18), supporting moderate oral bioavailability for the query's anilino-basic-amine scaffold; the single 1% table value (C13) is an outlier within that context.

The low-F records for selegiline (C02, C03, C06, C08, C09, C14, C16), rotigotine/N-0437 (C10, C17), and brexanolone (C20) depend on specific liabilities—propargyl/MAO metabolism, phenolic conjugation, and steroid scaffold—that are absent in the query, so they do not affirmatively establish F<20% for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule; the decision relies on transfer from analog contexts.
No query-specific data on first-pass metabolism, hepatic/intestinal clearance, or efflux are available.
The alfentanil context contains a conflicting 1% F record (C13), adding uncertainty to that analog.
The query is fully ionized at physiological pH (pKa 10.02), which could reduce passive permeability, but this physicochemical prior is not endpoint proof.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F>=20%) because the query's lipophilic basic diamine scaffold is best matched by amitriptyline (F ~40-60%) and alfentanil (F ~37-45%), while the low-F analogs carry specific metabolic liabilities absent in the query. Confidence is moderate because all evidence is transferred rather than measured directly.
